quizzes.stem: A team's monitoring shows its per-minute token use at about 40 percent of its tier's limit, yet 429 errors appear in sharp bursts whenever a scheduled job starts. Which explanation fits best?

options.a: Cached tokens are counted twice against the input limit, so the average hides the real total
options.b: The allowance resets in full at fixed minute boundaries, so jobs that start together all collide at once
options.c: Spare capacity is topped up gradually, so a sudden spike empties it even when the mean is low
options.d: A raised max_tokens value is charged against the output limit even when the reply is short

explanation.c: The limit works as a token bucket that is "continuously replenished up to your maximum limit", so a spike can empty it (module 12, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says that for most models "only uncached input tokens count toward ITPM", so cached tokens are not double counted.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the bucket refills "rather than being reset at fixed intervals", so there is no minute boundary.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the rate-limit page says "does not factor into OTPM rate limit calculations" for the max_tokens parameter.

quizzes.stem: After a provider update, a hand-written client that worked for months throws an exception on every reply because the JSON now carries a field it has never seen. Which change fits best?

options.a: Pin the request to an earlier documented version so replies keep their old shape
options.b: Pick out just the values the code uses and skip whatever else arrives
options.c: Validate every reply against a strict schema and reject anything that has an extra entry
options.d: Report the provider to support, because adding output values breaks the contract

explanation.b: A client should "Read what you need and ignore the rest", since an unknown field is not an error (module 13, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because earlier versions "may be unavailable for new users" and the only current value is the one already in use.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a client that fails on an unknown field "breaks on a change the versioning page allows".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the versioning policy reserves the right to "add additional values to the output", so nothing was broken.

quizzes.stem: A support bot caches a long prefix. After turn four the team wants a new tone rule applied to later turns on Claude Sonnet 5.5, without discarding the cached earlier part. Which two statements describe the approach that fits? (Select two.)

options.a: Rewrite the top-level system field with the new rule on the next request
options.b: Append a system-role instruction after the latest user message
options.c: End the list with a partial assistant message that already follows the rule
options.d: Prior content keeps its saved computation
options.e: Start a fresh conversation and resend a summary that includes the rule

explanation.b: A message with the system role after a user turn "does not invalidate a cached prefix that came before it" (module 14, page 1), so the earlier part of the conversation stays reusable.
explanation.d: A message with the system role after a user turn "does not invalidate a cached prefix that came before it" (module 14, page 1), so the earlier part of the conversation stays reusable.
explanation.a: Ruled out because adding the rule partway "changes the system prompt and invalidates the conversation's earlier thinking blocks".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a conversation that ends on the model's side "must end with a user message" and returns a 400.
explanation.e: Ruled out because the page assigns "the mid-conversation message for instructions that only become relevant later", so no restart is needed.

quizzes.stem: A dashboard charts only the plain input count from each response and shows 50 for a call that sent a 200,000-token document from the cache. The team asks whether the figure is broken. What should they be told?

options.a: The field was capped at 50 because the document exceeded the context limit of that model
options.b: Input tokens are billed separately from the cache, so the figure shown is already complete and exact
options.c: Streaming reports that figure only in the closing event, so the dashboard read it early
options.d: It holds just the tail after the final breakpoint, so combine it with the read and write totals

explanation.d: The plain count "only represents tokens that appear after your last cache breakpoint", so the other two fields must be added (module 14, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page gives the same case, "reads 50 although the total input is 200,050", and nothing was capped.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page states that "the total input is the sum of three numbers", not one.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says "the input side arrives in message_start", so timing does not explain a low value.

quizzes.stem: Every call returns a 400 whose message begins with "You have reached your specified API usage limits". The team reformats the request body three times with no change. What should they do next?

options.a: Back off and retry after the interval that the response supplies
options.b: Rotate the API key, since the credential has probably expired or been revoked
options.c: Raise the ceiling that an administrator configured below the plan's cap
options.d: Shrink the payload toward the 32 MB size limit and send it again

explanation.c: A limit set below the tier's cap returns a 400, and "Lifting the limit is the cure, not changing the request" (module 15, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a 400 is in the group where "the same request fails again", so waiting does not help.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page explains that "A limit you set yourself, below the tier's cap, also stops requests".
explanation.d: Ruled out because an oversized body gives a different outcome: "a larger request is refused with a 413".

quizzes.stem: A client computes a 2-second back-off after a rate-limit response, but that response carries a header asking for 30 seconds. Which delay should the client apply?

options.a: The computed value, because the header is only advisory
options.b: The longer of the two waits, because earlier retries will fail
options.c: The header value minus the time the failed request already took
options.d: Zero, so the limit is probed again as soon as it refills

explanation.b: The header sets a floor, so wait "the larger of your back-off and the header" (module 15, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "it is a floor, not a suggestion", so the header cannot be treated as advice.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the header text says "Earlier retries will fail", and nothing in it is reduced by elapsed time.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page warns that "hammering the endpoint in the meantime only fails".

quizzes.stem: A batch service must sustain 600 requests a minute against the API, and each call takes about 3 seconds. Which cap on simultaneous calls fits that target without inviting rate-limit errors?

options.a: About 10, the number of requests that begin during each single second
options.b: About 300, half of the requests that are sent during that minute
options.c: About 30, from the arrival frequency times each exchange's duration
options.d: About 600, one slot for each request sent during the minute

explanation.c: In-flight calls follow Little's law: "the number of requests in flight equals the request rate times the time each takes", so 10 a second for 3 seconds gives 30 (module 16, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page defines the bound as "the number of requests in flight equals the request rate times the time each takes", which includes the duration.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a bound above the need "would only invite 429 errors".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the rule is to "compute the bound from the limit you must stay under", not to match the total sent.

quizzes.stem: A logging layer for a streamed reply records the stop reason from the first chunk it receives and always stores a null. Which two statements explain it? (Select two.)

options.a: It arrives in the HTTP status line of the response
options.b: The value arrives in the delta frame sent close to the finish
options.c: It arrives in a content_block_stop frame, once each block completes
options.d: An interrupted transfer never delivers one
options.e: It arrives in message_start, alongside the input token count

explanation.b: The stop reason "arrives in message_delta, near the end", so a cut stream has none (module 17, page 1).
explanation.d: The stop reason "arrives in message_delta, near the end", so a cut stream has none (module 17, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "stop_reason indicates normal completion; HTTP errors indicate failures".
explanation.c: Ruled out because that frame means "The block at index is complete" and carries no reason.
explanation.e: Ruled out because the opening frame carries "an empty content and the input token count in usage", not the stop reason.

quizzes.stem: An operator stops a running batch and sees an interim state named canceling. What should the team expect for the requests that had already run?

options.a: Every one is refunded because the batch never reached its normal end
options.b: Their charges stand, and their outputs may show up once polling reaches the end
options.c: Their results are discarded and nothing can be downloaded afterwards
options.d: The whole batch is deleted at once, so its results address stops working for everyone

explanation.b: Batches that are stopped "end up with a status of ended and may contain partial results", and processed work is billed (module 21, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "the requests that had already run are still billed".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the batch "may contain partial results for requests that were processed before cancellation".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Cancellation may not be instant", so the batch is not removed at once.

quizzes.stem: A developer ports a working direct-API request to the Messages API of Claude in Amazon Bedrock and removes the version header, assuming the platform now handles versioning. What does the page say?

options.a: The date moves into the body and is renamed to a platform-specific field name
options.b: The platform infers it from the model identifier, so no value is sent
options.c: It stays, with the value 2023-06-01, exactly as on Anthropic's own endpoint
options.d: AWS signing replaces it, since SigV4 authenticates the whole call

explanation.c: On Bedrock the version "stays a header, as on the direct API" (module 22, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because that placement is the Google Cloud rule: "anthropic_version is passed in the request body".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the contract lists the version as "which the overview lists as required".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page treats them as separate items: "Authentication, version and body type are all a plain request needs".

quizzes.stem: A document-review service on Google Cloud attaches dozens of page images to each request and is refused although the token count is well under the window. Which limit did it most likely hit?

options.a: The 600-image ceiling that applies to models with larger windows
options.b: A payload size ceiling of 30 MB enforced by the platform
options.c: A tokens-per-minute quota that is shared across the account
options.d: A requirement that images arrive as links instead of encoded strings

explanation.b: Google Cloud "limits request payloads to 30 MB", which many images can reach first (module 22, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says the request size limit "can be reached first", before any image count.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the refusal came while the count was low, and a team with many images "can reach before the token limit".
explanation.d: Ruled out because on this platform "only base64-encoded sources are currently available", so links are not an option.

quizzes.stem: A security lead wants to stop all inference against foundation models in an AWS account today, while keeping the policy as short as possible. Which statement holds?

options.a: Each related action needs its own explicit deny statement as well
options.b: A wildcard in a deny rule is the same defect as one in an allow rule
options.c: Deny statements are ignored, so in practice only a narrow allow-list can remove access
options.d: Denying the invoke action alone also blocks the neighbouring conversation APIs

explanation.d: Denying InvokeModel is enough because other actions "are blocked automatically when InvokeModel is denied" (module 23, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page lists the neighbours, "such as Converse and StartAsyncInvoke", as blocked without extra statements.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "In a guardrail, the wildcard is the point", so the wildcard is legitimate in a deny.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a "statement belongs in a separate guardrail", which is where deny rules live.

quizzes.stem: A service that extracted invoices by forcing one tool on every call moves to Claude Sonnet 5.5 and every request now fails with a 400. Which replacement fits?

options.a: Switch the choice to any, which lets the model pick among the tools
options.b: A fixed-shape reply through the output format setting with a JSON schema
options.c: Ask for JSON in the prompt and parse whatever text comes back
options.d: Add an assistant message that opens a brace so that the reply begins as JSON

explanation.b: The page recommends structured outputs "when you need a response in a fixed JSON shape" (module 25, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because on these models `any` and `tool` "return a 400 error" just as a named tool does.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a prompt request gives "no guarantee; the program must parse defensively".
explanation.d: Ruled out because prefilled assistant messages "return a 400 error" on these models.

quizzes.stem: A team reads PDFs through Amazon Bedrock's Converse API and finds that answers ignore every chart, although the same files work well on the Claude API. Which two statements explain it and the fix? (Select two.)

options.a: Switching to base64 sources hides the links that blocked the images
options.b: A PDF surcharge disables page images unless it is paid
options.c: The visual mode requires citations enabled
options.d: Converting each PDF to plain text first adds the image content
options.e: Without them the service falls back to basic text extraction

explanation.c: "Without citations, Converse falls back to basic text extraction", so enabling them restores the full visual mode (module 30, page 2).
explanation.e: "Without citations, Converse falls back to basic text extraction", so enabling them restores the full visual mode (module 30, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because on that platform "only base64 sources are available", so that is already the case.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Standard API pricing applies with no additional PDF fees".
explanation.d: Ruled out because text extraction is the mode that "cannot analyze images or charts".

quizzes.stem: A guard hook works on its author's laptop but fails for every teammate who adds it from the marketplace; the command line names an absolute path. Which fix fits?

options.a: Copy the program into each teammate's home directory during onboarding
options.b: Move the guard into the agent file with a permission mode setting
options.c: Reach the program through the variable holding the install root
options.d: Place the program beside the manifest in the dot-folder

explanation.c: A hook script in a plugin "cannot assume where the plugin was installed", so it uses the plugin-root variable (module 39, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "The path differs on every machine", so a copied location cannot be shared.
explanation.b: Ruled out because agent fields of that kind "are ignored when loading agents from a plugin".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Only plugin.json goes inside .claude-plugin/", so other files do not belong there.

quizzes.stem: A workflow lets Claude push fixes to a branch, but the test pipeline that should run on each push never starts. The workflow signs in with the repository's built-in credential. Which change fits?

options.a: Commit with a GitHub App token, since the default one's commits trigger nothing
options.b: Pin the action to the beta tag so event delivery is restored
options.c: Grant the job write access to every scope, including the identity token
options.d: Limit parallel runs with concurrency controls so that the pipeline is not skipped over

explanation.a: "GitHub doesn't trigger workflows on commits made with the default GITHUB_TOKEN", so an app token is needed (module 40, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "workflows written for @beta need to move", which concerns versions and not triggers.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page tells you to "Grant the least a job needs".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "Use GitHub's concurrency controls to limit parallel runs", which bounds cost and does not trigger anything.

quizzes.stem: A team wrote its build commands and conventions into the repository's memory file while using the terminal tool. A developer now opens the same repository in an IDE extension. What should the team expect?

options.a: Nothing carries over, because each surface keeps its own separate memory
options.b: The conventions apply, but the settings and servers must be recreated
options.c: Only the terminal reads that file, and extensions need the Agent SDK
options.d: Matching rules and configuration apply, as each surface runs one engine

explanation.d: Each surface "connects to the same underlying Claude Code engine", so the files carry across (module 3, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "settings, and MCP servers work across all of them".
explanation.b: Ruled out because memory files "and settings that travel with the repository across its surfaces".
explanation.c: Ruled out because Claude Code is "available in the terminal, IDE extensions, a desktop app and the browser".

quizzes.stem: Nightly bulk jobs share a 30,000-token instruction block, yet cache hit rates stay low because each entry lapses before many requests have arrived. Which adjustment does the page suggest?

options.a: Submit that block as a separate batch beforehand to warm the entry
options.b: Ask for the one-hour lifetime on the common material
options.c: Remove the cache markers, because hits are impossible inside a batch
options.d: Vary the instruction block slightly per call so that entries differ

explanation.b: Because a batch can outlast five minutes, "it suggests the one-hour lifetime for shared context" (module 21, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because warming "targets time-to-first-token, which does not apply to batch processing".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says "The pricing discounts from prompt caching and Message Batches can stack".
explanation.d: Ruled out because hits depend on "identical cache_control blocks in every request".

quizzes.stem: A team began a long-running coding agent on the recommended default tier, and its own evaluations at higher effort still fall short of the quality bar. Which step fits the model overview?

options.a: Abandon the design, because no model suits long-horizon work of this kind
options.b: Add a second agent on the same tier so that answers receive a majority vote
options.c: Drop to Claude Sonnet 5.5, since faster models usually score higher on such tests
options.d: Switch to Claude Fable 5.1, which the page reserves for demanding reasoning

explanation.d: The overview points to Claude Fable 5.1 "when evals at higher effort still fall short" (module 3, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because Fable 5.1 is listed for "demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the course advises "adding complexity only when it demonstrably improves outcomes".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the method is to "move down a tier at a time until quality drops", which comes after the target is met.

quizzes.stem: A shared request builder sends Claude Sonnet 5.5 a thinking setting that keeps only the short updates between tool calls, together with xhigh effort, and every call returns a 400. Which two statements explain it and the fix? (Select two.)

options.a: That mode works at the three lowest levels
options.b: Pass adaptive as the effort value so that the model chooses its own
options.c: Raise max_tokens, because the 400 reports a truncated reply
options.d: Add temperature 0 so that the behaviour becomes deterministic
options.e: At the two highest levels it is rejected

explanation.a: The mode "works at `low`, `medium` and `high` effort and returns a 400 at `xhigh` and `max`" (module 19, page 1), so the fix is one of the three lowest values.
explanation.e: The mode "works at `low`, `medium` and `high` effort and returns a 400 at `xhigh` and `max`" (module 19, page 1), so the fix is one of the three lowest values.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Don't pass adaptive as an effort value".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a cut reply is a different case, because it "arrives with status 200".
explanation.d: Ruled out because on these models "a non-default value of any of them is rejected with a 400 error".

quizzes.stem: After a deploy, a service immediately fires ten simultaneous requests that share a 30,000-token prefix with a marker on it. Usage shows ten writes and no reads. What is the fix?

options.a: Raise the lifetime to one hour so later entries reach the earlier one
options.b: Alternate the effort setting on every call to spread out the writes
options.c: Send one, wait until its response begins, then release the other nine
options.d: Shrink the prefix below the minimum so that nothing has to be written

explanation.c: The page says to "wait for the first response before sending subsequent requests" (module 20, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a one-hour entry "writes at twice the base price" and still does not exist before the first response.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Changing the thinking mode or the effort always discards the cached messages".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a prefix below the minimum "will be processed without caching", so the saving is lost.

quizzes.stem: A team has no evaluation data yet and no sense of how hard its new feature is. Which starting plan matches the documentation's method?

options.a: Pick the cheapest tier at once, since the pricing page says to use it for simple tasks
options.b: Begin with a capable model, test on real cases, then step down a tier at a time
options.c: Use the top tier permanently, since it protects quality for every task
options.d: Choose by reputation, then adjust after the first production complaint

explanation.b: The method is to "measure on your own cases, then move down a tier at a time" (module 18, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the first step is to "start high, so that a failure means the task is hard".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the course notes that nothing "says the biggest model is the safest default for every task".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A tier is right only if it passed your evaluation at the lowest cost".

quizzes.stem: A request to Claude Haiku 4.5, whose limit is 200K, carries about 150,000 input tokens and sets max_tokens to 64,000, which together go beyond that limit. What happens?

options.a: The call is accepted, and a lengthy reply may end early with a dedicated stop reason
options.b: The call is rejected with a 400, because input plus output may not exceed the limit
options.c: The excess is trimmed from the start of the input history before any processing begins
options.d: The output allowance is silently lowered to fit, so the reply always completes

explanation.a: Input plus max_tokens beyond the window is allowed because "the request is still accepted", and generation stops at the limit (module 1, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Older models returned a validation error instead".
explanation.c: Ruled out because chat products "manage the window on a rolling first-in, first-out basis; the API does not".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "if generation then reaches the window limit it stops with" a stop reason, not a lowered allowance.

quizzes.stem: Two otherwise identical multi-turn services use thinking: one runs on Claude Opus 5.5 and one on Claude Haiku 4.5. The first one's conversations fill their context faster. Which two statements explain the gap? (Select two.)

options.a: Haiku 4.5 has a smaller window of 64K, so its context is cleared sooner
options.b: Adaptive thinking bills reasoning as input, which crowds the window
options.c: The larger model retains earlier reasoning by default
options.d: Opus 5.5 can disable thinking, so it compensates with longer prompts
options.e: The smaller model drops earlier reasoning blocks

explanation.c: Earlier thinking is kept where "current Opus, Sonnet, Fable models keep them by default" (module 4, page 2), and the smaller model strips it, which is why the first service's context fills faster.
explanation.e: Earlier thinking is kept where "current Opus, Sonnet, Fable models keep them by default" (module 4, page 2), and the smaller model strips it, which is why the first service's context fills faster.
explanation.a: Ruled out because Haiku 4.5 has a window of "200K for Claude Haiku 4.5", and 64K is only its output ceiling.
explanation.b: Ruled out because reasoning tokens "are billed as output tokens".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Opus 5.5 use adaptive thinking that is always on".

quizzes.stem: A drafting feature scores 62 percent on the team's fixed test set against a 90 percent target and costs more than planned. Someone proposes switching tiers immediately. What does the module advise?

options.a: Switch tiers now, since a lower price makes later quality work affordable
options.b: Judge the lower tier on the ten easiest items, then roll it out
options.c: Rewrite several parts of the prompt together to gain accuracy quickly
options.d: Hit the quality bar before looking for any saving that holds it

explanation.d: The order is "first reach the quality bar; then look for the cheaper way to hold it" (module 6, page 4).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a smaller tier fits only "where the evaluation set says quality holds".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says to "Test the cheap tier first on the hard cases, not on the easy ones".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Several simultaneous edits leave you unable to say what helped".

quizzes.stem: A team migrates a reasoning-heavy workload to a newer model and copies its old effort values unchanged. Quality drifts. Which step does the guidance give?

options.a: Reapply the old thinking budgets, which carry over between generations
options.b: Run a sweep across levels on its own test set
options.c: Raise every level by one notch, since newer models think less per level
options.d: Pin the old model id until the next generation arrives

explanation.b: The page says to "Run an effort sweep on your own evals rather than carrying settings over from an earlier model" (module 18, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a manual budget "or a manual budget_tokens, is rejected" on the newer models.
explanation.c: Ruled out because on Sonnet 5.5 "its levels are recalibrated", so no direction can be assumed.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page promises "at least 60 days' notice before model retirement", which allows time to test instead of waiting.

quizzes.stem: A pipeline starts two model calls at once: one drafts a reply and one checks the reply's tone, but the checker keeps failing because the draft does not exist yet. How should the team restructure it?

options.a: Run them in sequence, so the second receives the first one's output
options.b: Vote across three identical drafting calls, then check the winner
options.c: Route the draft to a specialised prompt chosen by a classifier
options.d: Replace both calls with an autonomous agent that decides the order of the steps

explanation.a: Sectioning needs independent work, and "Parallel calls cannot see each other's output", so a dependent step belongs in a chain (module 34, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because sectioning means "independent subtasks run in parallel", which these are not.
explanation.c: Ruled out because routing "directs it to a specialized followup task" and does not order two calls.
explanation.d: Ruled out because an agent suits a case where "the path cannot be written in advance", and this path is fixed.

quizzes.stem: In a draft-and-review loop, the reviewer's reply is sometimes prose such as "looks fine to me" instead of a score the program can parse. The loop currently treats that as a pass. What should it do?

options.a: Accept it as a pass, since no objection was raised
options.b: Count the attempt as unchecked, giving it zero with a stated cause
options.c: Pull the first digit from the text and treat it as the grade
options.d: Return the latest draft, since the reviewer is evidently satisfied

explanation.b: "If the verdict cannot be parsed, the draft is unchecked", so it is graded zero with a reason (module 34, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a reply that is not a bare score counts as ungradable", and an ungradable case fails.
explanation.c: Ruled out because such a parse "turns a broken grader into a plausible number".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A refinement loop can get worse", so the page keeps the best draft and not the last.

quizzes.stem: A service sets a dollar budget on its Agent SDK run, and the run fans work out to secondary workers. Finance worries that the workers' spending escapes the limit. What does the documentation say?

options.a: No cost control exists, so the team must stop runs by hand
options.b: The cap counts only turns that use a tool, never dollars
options.c: The cap is checked once the run finishes, so overruns are unavoidable
options.d: The ceiling reaches down to the delegates as well

explanation.d: The page states that "the budget covers subagents too" (module 35, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the option is described as "Maximum cost before stopping".
explanation.b: Ruled out because only the turn limit "counts tool-use turns only", while the budget measures cost.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "When a limit is reached the run ends with a result whose subtype names it".

quizzes.stem: A custom in-process tool is annotated as read-only, and the team lets it run alongside other tools without review, assuming that it cannot modify anything. Which two statements explain why that assumption fails? (Select two.)

options.a: The handler's code can still write
options.b: The label is enforced when the tool is served from outside the process boundary
options.c: The SDK rejects any write that such a tool attempts while the run is under way
options.d: Tools carrying the label are always run one at a time, to stay on the safe side
options.e: The label is scheduling metadata and not a guarantee

explanation.a: "Annotations are metadata, not enforcement", and "A tool marked read-only can still write if its handler does" (module 35, page 2).
explanation.e: "Annotations are metadata, not enforcement", and "A tool marked read-only can still write if its handler does" (module 35, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because clients treat annotations as "untrusted unless they come from trusted servers", wherever the tool is served.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Annotations are metadata, not enforcement".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the hint "lets the tool run in parallel with other read-only tools".

quizzes.stem: A team promotes a new system prompt for a hosted agent and wants production runs to keep the previous behaviour until a person approves the switch. Which approach fits?

options.a: Override the system field on every run, since overrides merge with the saved agent
options.b: Create the sessions with just the agent ID, which pins the first version
options.c: Create each session with a pinned version number
options.d: Edit the agent in place, because environments are versioned for rollback

explanation.c: The page says "a session can instead pin a version" so a prompt can be promoted or rolled back without a deploy (module 36, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "overrides replace and never merge".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a session made with just an agent ID "creates the session with the latest agent version".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Environments are not versioned".

quizzes.stem: A security officer approves self-hosted sandboxes for a managed agent on the grounds that nothing the agent touches will ever leave the company network. What is wrong with that reasoning?

options.a: Inputs and outputs of each call still reach the provider's control plane
options.b: Only the sandbox image is hosted by the provider, so source files are exposed
options.c: Files and processes also run on the provider's side, so only egress rules differ
options.d: The environment key must be stored inside the image so the worker can start

explanation.a: "Tool inputs and outputs still flow to Anthropic's control plane" (module 36, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Anthropic does not inspect or verify your sandbox image", and the image is the customer's.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says "files, processes and network traffic stay in your environment".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the key belongs in "a secrets manager, never an image".

quizzes.stem: A typed agent returns a refund record that passes its schema, showing an amount of 4999 cents for a 49-cent item, and the team ships it because validation succeeded. What should they conclude?

options.a: The schema is wrong, because a correct type guarantees a correct number
options.b: Form checks prove only the shape, so a separate rule must judge the value
options.c: The retry loop should have caught it, since failed validation retries by itself
options.d: A graph framework would have prevented it, since its checkpoints verify values

explanation.b: "Validation proves the shape", and nothing more (module 37, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A refund of 4999 cents passes the schema whether or not it is right".
explanation.c: Ruled out because only "a reply that does not validate against the output type is refused", and this one validated.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A checkpoint is a copy of the state at a point in the graph", not a check.

quizzes.stem: A team wants a framework mainly because it is popular, though nobody can say which missing feature it would supply. Which step does the page advise?

options.a: Write the requirement with a number in it and test the simplest option
options.b: Adopt it and trim the unused parts after the first release goes out
options.c: Count the features each candidate offers and pick the longest list of them
options.d: Pick the family by the brand that has published the most releases

explanation.a: The page says to "check whether the simplest option meets it" (module 37, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the advice is to "start with direct calls and add layers when a need appears".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A framework that offers persistence helps only when the product must resume".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The question is who should own the route, not which library is popular".

quizzes.stem: An application pastes a user's forwarded email between fixed tags in its prompt. A tester shows that an email containing the closing tag followed by new orders is treated as part of the instructions. Which measure from the page on pasted content fits best?

options.a: Move the email above the instructions so that its position marks it as data
options.b: Place the email in the system prompt, where it carries the most weight with the model
options.c: Fence it with a random identifier and warn the model it could hold directives
options.d: Rely on tags alone, because the model treats text inside tags as inert data

explanation.c: The page wraps pasted text in a tag "with a random id that your application generates" and says the text may carry instructions (module 24, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Moving a pasted document above the instructions does not mark it as data".
explanation.b: Ruled out because data in the system prompt "gets the authority of an instruction".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Tags mark where data starts and ends, but they do not make data safe".

quizzes.stem: A JSON schema for a classifier includes a property named "thinking_steps" that demands the model's reasoning, and some requests now come back refused. Which change fits?

options.a: Raise max_tokens so that the long reasoning is not cut off
options.b: Retry the same call until the model stops refusing
options.c: Lower the effort so the model reasons less before filling the field
options.d: Ask for a brief explanation in its place

explanation.d: The page says to "Ask for a short explanation instead" of the reasoning (module 24, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a 200 with refusal is not an answer", and a refusal is not a cut reply.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The same request gets the same decision".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says "Do not ask for the reasoning as output", whatever the effort.

quizzes.stem: An extraction loop repairs failed replies by sending the original prompt again with the note "try again". The same mistakes keep recurring. Which two changes fit? (Select two.)

options.a: Retry without a limit, since eventual success is likely on a hard document
options.b: Return the model's own answer with the request
options.c: List every problem with its path and message
options.d: Add a prefilled assistant turn that opens the JSON object
options.e: Report only the first problem each time, to keep the note short

explanation.b: The next call needs the model's own reply and "a user message that lists each problem with its path and message" (module 25, page 2).
explanation.c: The next call needs the model's own reply and "a user message that lists each problem with its path and message" (module 25, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "An unbounded retry on a hard document is a cost leak".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Prefilling the assistant response returns a 400 error" on current models.
explanation.e: Ruled out because "Collect all the problems in one pass".

quizzes.stem: A retrieval service embeds both stored passages and incoming questions with the same provider call and no further options, and results are mediocre. Which change do the course pages back?

options.a: Truncate each passage to a single sentence before embedding
options.b: Switch to Anthropic's own embedding model, which handles both uses
options.c: Set the parameter that labels each input as a query or a document
options.d: Replace the vectors with keyword scores, which match meaning exactly

explanation.c: The documentation says "Do not omit input_type or set input_type=None" (module 28, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Too small a chunk loses context".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Anthropic does not offer its own embedding model".
explanation.d: Ruled out because keyword scoring fails on paraphrases because "it matches words, not meaning".

quizzes.stem: An agent compacts its history every forty turns by adding a fresh summary, and after several rounds the conversation holds four summaries that partly contradict each other. Which fix fits?

options.a: Keep every summary and let the newest override the rest
options.b: Delete the oldest summary and keep the other three
options.c: Stop compacting and raise max_tokens to avoid a full window
options.d: Fold the earlier one into the newest, leaving exactly one

explanation.d: "A second compaction should fold the first summary into the new one", so that exactly one remains (module 29, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "exactly one block is sent per request".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "an earlier summary is folded into the next one rather than stacked".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Raising it does not enlarge the window".

quizzes.stem: A team enables automatic clearing of old tool results, yet every clearing frees only a few hundred tokens and the next request pays a large cache write. Which parameter addresses this?

options.a: A longer list of excluded tools so fewer results qualify
options.b: A higher keep value so more recent pairs stay
options.c: A lower bound on the savings each pass must achieve
options.d: A lower trigger so that clearing begins at a smaller context size

explanation.c: The setting exists for the cache, because clearing "invalidates cached prompt prefixes when content is cleared" (module 29, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because exclusions are "tool names whose results are never cleared", which makes clears smaller.
explanation.b: Ruled out because keep sets "how many recent tool use and result pairs stay", which shrinks each clear further.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the trigger sets "when clearing starts; input_tokens or tool_uses" and not how much each pass frees.

quizzes.stem: A service forces a named tool on Claude Haiku 4.5 and every reply is a bare tool call with no sentence before it, but product wants a brief explanation first. What fits?

options.a: Switch to the any setting, which adds an explanation before the call
options.b: Disable parallel use, since one action per reply lets text appear first
options.c: Set the choice to none so that commentary is written before anything else
options.d: Use the automatic setting and say in a user message to run that function

explanation.d: The page says "To get both a tool call and an explanation, use auto and say in a user message to use the tool" (module 26, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the API prefills the assistant message to force a tool to be used", so no text comes first.
explanation.b: Ruled out because with a forced type "Claude calls exactly one tool", and no text is promised.
explanation.c: Ruled out because none "prevents Claude from using any tools".

quizzes.stem: After a refactor, a model that used to call three independent tools in one reply now calls them one at a time. The code sends each output back in its own message. What is the likely cause?

options.a: Parallel use is limited to operations that merely read data, so that setting changed
options.b: The default for the choice field was switched to disable parallel use between releases
options.c: Separate returns teach Claude to avoid issuing several requests together
options.d: Parallel calls vanish whenever a conversation passes a certain length of history

explanation.c: The rule is to "return one tool_result for each tool_use block, all together in the next user message" (module 26, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "By default, Claude may call multiple tools in a single response".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the switch is a field of the choice object: "It is not a top-level request parameter".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The most common issue is formatting tool results incorrectly in the conversation history".

quizzes.stem: A developer connects forty tool-bearing servers to Claude Code and worries that every request now carries all their schemas. Which two statements does the documentation support? (Select two.)

options.a: Dormant integrations cost little space
options.b: Discovery on demand is switched on by default
options.c: The schemas belong in CLAUDE.md, which loads when a question needs them
options.d: Servers load nothing at start, so adding more affects latency alone
options.e: Each schema loads in full at session start, so the cost stays fixed per server

explanation.a: "Tool search is on by default, so idle MCP tools consume minimal context" (module 27, page 1).
explanation.b: "Tool search is on by default, so idle MCP tools consume minimal context" (module 27, page 1).
explanation.c: Ruled out because "CLAUDE.md is paid for on every request".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the context cost is "low until a tool is used", and not zero.
explanation.e: Ruled out because the loading table shows "tool names; full schemas on demand".

quizzes.stem: An application defines its own function called screenshot alongside Anthropic's screen-control entry. Incoming blocks with that word are sometimes meant for one and sometimes for the other. How should dispatch work?

options.a: Reject the custom function, because member names are reserved
options.b: Use the order in which the blocks arrive to decide which handler applies
options.c: Check whether the block carries display dimensions, which only screen actions have
options.d: Branch on the member together with the extra field that identifies the toolset

explanation.d: "toolset_name is what marks a block as a computer action" (module 31, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A custom tool in the same request can share a member's name".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says to "Dispatch on the pair" of member and field, not on arrival order.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The entry takes no display size", so blocks carry no dimensions.

quizzes.stem: A Python MCP server rejects a blank title by raising an ordinary ValueError inside the handler, and the model never sees why the call failed. Which change fits?

options.a: Return a protocol error, since the model can retry after a malformed request
options.b: Print the reason to standard output so that the client can relay it
options.c: Signal it with the SDK's dedicated exception type for expected problems
options.d: Catch the exception and return an empty success result

explanation.c: "In the Python SDK, raise ToolError for an expected failure" (module 32, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because protocol errors are for "issues with the request structure itself that models are less likely to be able to fix".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a swallowed failure "tells the model the call worked".

quizzes.stem: During a deployment tool's confirmation step, the person chooses decline. The server currently returns a protocol error and the client logs an incident. How should the server treat that answer?

options.a: As a failed call, signalling the code for a missing client capability
options.b: As an ordinary outcome, finishing with a result that reports it was cancelled
options.c: As a prompt to ask again, repeating the confirmation until the person accepts
options.d: As a timeout, so the whole call is retried with a new identifier

explanation.b: "An answer of decline or cancel is a normal outcome" (module 33, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because that error is for a capability the call did not declare, "which names the missing capabilities".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page lists three forms of answer and says "a server handles each".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a retry exists to supply information: the client "retries the original request including the additional requested information".

quizzes.stem: A company on a commercial plan, with training use off by default, tells staff that anything typed is erased within 30 days. A reviewer notes one exception that staff create themselves. Which action does the reviewer mean?

options.a: Giving thumbs feedback on a reply keeps the conversation for up to five years
options.b: Opening a chat in incognito mode, which is then stored by the provider for a year
options.c: Connecting a data source, whose raw content is then kept by the provider for seven years
options.d: Deleting a chat, which the back end then retains for five years in a hidden archive

explanation.a: "Giving feedback with the thumbs buttons stores the conversation for up to five years", on both plan types (module 10, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Incognito chats are not used to improve Claude".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Raw content fetched through a connector is excluded unless you copy it into the chat".
explanation.d: Ruled out because where improvement is off, "a deleted chat leaves the back end within 30 days".

quizzes.stem: A team plans to drop the disposable container for its screen-driving agent because Anthropic already scans screenshots for planted instructions. Which two statements should the reviewer make? (Select two.)

options.a: Injected text can still be obeyed despite the filter
options.b: Screenshots are processed by Anthropic alone, so no local safeguards apply
options.c: Such filters are a backup layer behind the first defences
options.d: Dropping the container is fine once an allowlist of domains is in place
options.e: The scan makes planted text harmless, so the confirmation steps can go too

explanation.a: The classifiers "are a second layer", and "Claude will follow commands found in content even when they conflict with your instructions" (module 31, page 2).
explanation.c: The classifiers "are a second layer", and "Claude will follow commands found in content even when they conflict with your instructions" (module 31, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because screenshots "are captured and stored in your environment, not by Anthropic".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the precautions begin with "a dedicated virtual machine or container with minimal privileges".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "They are a second layer", behind the container, the missing secrets, the allowlist and the confirmation.

quizzes.stem: An agent loop returns a vendor lookup to Claude, and the team adds "now email the summary to finance" to the end of that same return. The instruction is routinely ignored. Which placement fits?

options.a: Put it in a separate user message that follows the block
options.b: Repeat it three times inside the returned text so it is noticed
options.c: Move it into the system prompt together with the vendor text
options.d: Wrap it in a JSON string with the vendor data so both stay together

explanation.a: The page says "Don't put your own instructions in tool results", so send them in a user turn after the block (module 41, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Claude treats that content as untrusted data, so your instruction may be ignored", however often it is repeated.
explanation.c: Ruled out because third-party content goes "never in system prompts or plain user text blocks".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the JSON step applies to untrusted content: "Wrap third-party strings in a JSON object".

quizzes.stem: A screening call on a web fetch's raw output flags an injection attempt. The agent loop currently passes the page through anyway and logs a warning. What does the documentation say to return?

options.a: The untouched page, plus a note telling the model that it looks suspect
options.b: Nothing at all, ending the whole run immediately with no output
options.c: A failure notice or a condensed digest rather than the original body
options.d: The page with the matched phrases deleted and the rest left intact

explanation.c: The page says to "return an error or a stripped summary in the tool_result block instead of the raw content" (module 41, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because content is returned only "if the screen reports no injection attempt".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page adds "consider surfacing the attempt to the user", which is not a reason to end the run.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A list of patterns catches the phrasing someone thought of and misses the paraphrase".

quizzes.stem: A CI job runs the headless mode with the flag that skips local configuration and now reports no credentials, although the developer is signed in with a subscription on the same machine. What is needed?

options.a: Mount the developer's keychain into the runner so it can be read
options.b: Drop the flag, since the other mode sees the same local setup on every machine
options.c: Run it interactively in a terminal, where the login prompt can appear
options.d: Provide an API key through the environment

explanation.d: Bare mode "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain", so a key must come from the environment (module 38, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because bare mode "never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain", so mounting it changes nothing.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the flag is "useful for CI and scripts where you need the same result on every machine".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the headless mode is meant to "Run Claude non-interactively for CI, pre-commit hooks, or batch processing".

quizzes.stem: Two hooks match the same shell call: a logging hook that exits cleanly and a guard hook that answers with a denial. A teammate fears the logger's success will let the call through. What happens?

options.a: It proceeds, because the hook that exits with zero is consulted first
options.b: It is stopped, since the harshest verdict among them prevails
options.c: It proceeds, since hooks run one after another and the first result decides
options.d: It pauses for a person, because any disagreement produces an ask

explanation.b: When several hooks match, "the most restrictive answer applies", so the denial wins (module 39, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A logging hook that exits 0 does not weaken a guard hook that denies".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Several hooks can match one call, and they run in parallel".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the order is "in the order deny, defer, ask, allow", so deny outranks ask.

quizzes.stem: Between two evaluation runs the pass rate rose from 0.71 to 0.80, but a diff shows that four failing cases were deleted from the set. How should the harness treat this?

options.a: Flag the dropped items as removed and reject the check
options.b: Accept it, since a higher pass rate means the change helped
options.c: Treat the deleted ones as passes, since nothing contradicts them
options.d: Ignore the deletions when the edge-tagged cases still reach their threshold

explanation.a: The harness "reports it as removed and fails the comparison" (module 42, page 3).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "An average never excuses a regression".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A case that disappears is not a pass".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "dropping the case that fails is the easiest way to improve a score".

quizzes.stem: A support console's spec says that no summary may repeat a card number found in a ticket thread, and the team must decide where that rule is enforced. Which approach fits best?

options.a: A firm instruction in the prompt, written in capitals and repeated twice at the top
options.b: A target that at least 90 percent of summaries are rated accurate by two leads
options.c: A regular expression in the application code that screens each output before display
options.d: A longer explanation of the rule, placed in the user turn of every request

explanation.c: A guarantee that must always hold "belongs in code, not in a prompt", so the screening runs on every output (module 12, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a rule such as never output a card number "is only a request to the model".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a quality target is "stated as a rate over a set of examples", which tolerates misses, while this rule must hold for every summary.
explanation.d: Ruled out because wording in any turn only raises the odds, since "it cannot make it certain".

quizzes.stem: A team wants an alert that fires before its first 429 arrives, not after. Which signal fits best?

options.a: The remaining allowance that the headers report for requests and tokens
options.b: The count of 5xx errors per hour, which reflects the provider's capacity
options.c: The count of 400 replies per hour, which reflects the load on the service
options.d: The latency percentile at the edge of the service, compared with the budget

explanation.a: The headers report the remaining allowance, "so you can alert before the first 429" (module 12, page 3).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a rise in 5xx is a provider story", not a sign of your own headroom.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a rise in 400s is a bug in your requests", and says nothing about the allowance left.
explanation.d: Ruled out because latency is a separate signal, while "Headroom against the limits" is the one that warns before a 429.

quizzes.stem: A Python service uses the official SDK and now needs the rate-limit headers of each reply, which the typed return value does not expose. Which route fits best?

options.a: Replace the SDK with a hand-written client that sets three headers on every request
options.b: Turn on debug logging and read the headers out of the log output
options.c: Read the usage fields of each reply, which hold the remaining allowance
options.d: Make the request through the raw-response accessor and parse the result afterwards

explanation.d: The SDK offers a raw-response accessor in Python that gives the headers first, then the parsed object, because "each SDK has an escape hatch" (module 13, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the SDK is not wrong here, since "Each SDK has an escape hatch" for exactly this need.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Debug logging is a development tool", and bodies stay visible in it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the usage fields report "what the call consumed", not the allowance that is left.

quizzes.stem: A hand-written reader for streamed replies waits for a final data line reading [DONE] and hangs on every call. Which two statements explain it? (Select two.)

options.a: A longer read timeout lets the missing line finally arrive
options.b: The format uses only named events
options.c: A websocket is needed to signal the end of a reply
options.d: A keep-alive ping is what normally marks the end of a reply
options.e: The old closing marker no longer exists

explanation.b: The page records that "All events are named events" in the version the API uses, and "the old data: [DONE] marker is gone", so the end of a reply is a named event (module 13, page 3).
explanation.e: The page records that "All events are named events" in the version the API uses, and "the old data: [DONE] marker is gone", so the end of a reply is a named event (module 13, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the old data: [DONE] marker is gone", so no amount of waiting will bring it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The Messages API does not need it".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a ping is "a keep-alive with no content", and it does not mark the end.

quizzes.stem: After a tool loop, Claude Sonnet 5.5 sometimes ends its turn with no content at all. The client packs each tool's findings into the message together with a sentence announcing that data is attached. Which change fits best?

options.a: Raise max_tokens so that the model has room to produce a full answer
options.b: Retry the identical request until a non-empty reply finally arrives
options.c: Send the result blocks alone, with no text of any kind placed beside them
options.d: Switch the request to streaming so the empty turn is delivered in pieces

explanation.c: Text added next to the results "teaches Claude to expect user input after every tool use", so the results go alone (module 14, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because an empty reply with end_turn "is almost always self-inflicted", and a larger ceiling does not touch the cause.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Don't retry empty responses without modification".
explanation.d: Ruled out because streaming only "changes when the bytes arrive", not what the model produces.

quizzes.stem: A chat form lets a person submit an empty message, and each one still triggers a paid call whose reply wanders. Which handling fits best?

options.a: Refuse the blank turn in the client, before anything is sent over the network
options.b: Send it anyway and discard the reply when it comes back from the service
options.c: Insert a default question in place of the blank so that the call is useful
options.d: Add a line to the system prompt telling Claude to ignore empty messages

explanation.a: The page says an empty user turn is a wasted call, so "refuse it before anything is sent" (module 14, page 3).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "An empty user turn is a wasted call at best", and discarding the reply does not save the cost.
explanation.c: Ruled out because that makes "a different conversation from the one the user sees".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A sentence in a prompt can make a behaviour much more likely", but the call is still paid for.

quizzes.stem: A service decides whether to retry by searching the error message for the word overloaded. After the provider rewords the message, retries stop. Which change fits best?

options.a: Add the provider's new wording to the search and keep matching on the message text
options.b: Retry every error for ten minutes whatever its status
options.c: Catch only the SDK's base class, so that every failure takes one path
options.d: Branch on the status and type through the SDK's typed classes, most specific first

explanation.d: The documentation says to "catch the SDK's typed classes rather than string-matching error messages" (module 15, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a message can be reworded without notice", so the same break will return.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a 400, 401, 404 or 413 "returns the same answer each time".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the base class is kept "as a last resort", after the most specific classes.

quizzes.stem: A team streams five-minute reports and sets a read timeout of 30 seconds, worried that long generations will always trip it. What should the review say?

options.a: It will trip, because the limit covers the whole generation from its very first byte
options.b: The clock restarts at every event, so steady output survives and only a stall fails
options.c: It will fail unless the timeout is raised to the ten-minute default
options.d: The timeout applies only before the first byte, so it never matters afterwards

explanation.b: "a long generation that is steadily producing text does not hit a short read timeout" (module 15, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because for a streamed reply "the clock restarts with every event", so the whole generation is not one interval.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Streaming changes the arithmetic in your favour", so a short limit can stay.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the read clock measures "how long to wait between bytes of the reply".

quizzes.stem: A service sends the same 30,000-token instruction block with every request and reaches its input-token ceiling long before its request ceiling. Which two statements describe the cause and the lever? (Select two.)

options.a: Reads from a cache are left out of that count
options.b: Routing through a second inference geography adds a separate rate pool
options.c: A second workspace raises the organisation's overall allowance
options.d: Marking the shared prefix for reuse raises throughput
options.e: Raising max_tokens gives each reply more output per call

explanation.a: "Only uncached input counts toward ITPM" for most models, so cache reads free capacity (module 16, page 2).
explanation.d: "Only uncached input counts toward ITPM" for most models, so cache reads free capacity (module 16, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Rate limits are shared across all inference_geo values".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "organisation limits always apply" whatever the workspace.
explanation.e: Ruled out because the setting "does not factor into OTPM rate limit calculations", and the pressure is on input.

quizzes.stem: An assembler for streamed replies joins `thinking_delta` fragments into the thinking text but discards the `signature_delta` events as noise. Which two statements describe what it should do? (Select two.)

options.a: That attribute must travel back unmodified
options.b: Regenerate the value locally from a hash of the thinking text
options.c: Ignore them, since only the text deltas matter for the final message
options.d: Their payload becomes an attribute of the block
options.e: Append their text to the end of the thinking text

explanation.a: A signature "must be sent back unchanged with the thinking block" (module 17, page 1), and a signature_delta sets it.
explanation.d: A signature "must be sent back unchanged with the thinking block" (module 17, page 1), and a signature_delta sets it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "thinking or redacted_thinking blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the rule to "ignore event types you do not know" covers unknown types, and this one is documented.
explanation.e: Ruled out because "a signature_delta sets the signature", and it does not extend the thinking.

quizzes.stem: A background service sets a very large max_tokens, and the SDK refuses its non-streaming request before sending it. Nobody watches the output, the answer is needed within minutes, and the team wants the least extra code. Which option fits best?

options.a: Write an event handler of your own that assembles each content block as it arrives
options.b: Lower max_tokens until the request passes the size check and goes out
options.c: Use the final-message helper, which relies on events internally and returns one message
options.d: Move the request into a batch, whose results arrive together as one file

explanation.c: The helpers "stream underneath and return one message", so a long call needs no event handling (module 17, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a long call "does not need the event handling in your own code".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the refusal is a hint, since "if you see it, you wanted streaming".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a batch does not fit "work needed within the hour".

quizzes.stem: A team's list holds 1,000 request ids and the result file has 998 lines, yet its program reports every request as handled. What should it do?

options.a: Treat the missing two as succeeded, since nothing in the file contradicts them
options.b: Diff the sent identifiers against the returned ones and resend any that are missing
options.c: Resubmit the whole batch, since a short result file means that processing has failed
options.d: Match the two by position, since the file keeps the order of submission

explanation.b: The page says to "compare the ids you sent with the ids you received" (module 21, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a request without a result line is a gap", not a success.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the failure of one request in a batch does not affect the processing of other requests".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Batch results can be returned in any order".

quizzes.stem: A team on Google Cloud wants to reference a PDF by its web address in each request instead of embedding it. What do the platform pages say?

options.a: Web addresses work there, and a PDF counts as a document block like any other
options.b: Web addresses do not work there for documents, though they do for images
options.c: A single upload through the Files API lets later requests reference the PDF by id
options.d: That source type is not offered there, so another way to supply the file is needed

explanation.d: The Google Cloud list of gaps includes "Input sources (URL sources for images and documents, Files API)" (module 22, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the gap list names "URL sources for images and documents", so documents are excluded.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the missing item covers "URL sources for images and documents" together.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the table shows "Files API | yes | no | no", so it is missing there too.

quizzes.stem: A team calls Claude Sonnet 5.5 through Amazon Bedrock with valid credentials and a correct policy, yet the call is refused. Which prerequisite does the page name?

options.a: The model must first be enabled for the account, since access is gated per model
options.b: A quota request to Anthropic, because new accounts start with zero tokens per minute
options.c: Request logging must be on, because Bedrock refuses calls that are not logged
options.d: A Model Garden model card must be opened first, as on Google Cloud

explanation.a: "Amazon Bedrock sets access criteria for each Claude model individually" (module 23, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)", so a quota is already in place.
explanation.c: Ruled out because Anthropic only "recommends retaining activity logs on at least a 30-day rolling basis".
explanation.d: Ruled out because that is the Google route: "go to its Model Garden model card".

quizzes.stem: A prompt asks Claude to return each box as percentages of the picture, and the boxes land in the wrong places. Which change fits best?

options.a: Pad every picture to a multiple of 28 pixels before sending it
options.b: Divide each returned point by the padded size to obtain the fractions
options.c: Request pixel coordinates, then convert them to ratios in the program
options.d: Upload the image through the Files API so that its coordinates are kept

explanation.c: "Claude does not work well when you ask for normalized coordinates", so the program normalises (module 30, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Claude then pads every image on the bottom and right up to a multiple of 28" by itself.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Always normalize or rescale by the resized dimensions, not the padded dimensions".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "every box and point it returns is in that size and not in yours", whatever the source type.

quizzes.stem: A team member keeps a skill called deploy in the user-level skills location, and the repository commits a skill with the same name. Which one runs in a session there?

options.a: The repository's copy, because committed files take precedence
options.b: The developer's own copy, since that scope outranks the project's
options.c: Neither one, because Claude asks which to use when the names collide
options.d: Both in turn, with the project steps appended after the personal ones

explanation.b: The order is "Enterprise over personal, and personal over project" (module 39, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because committing only shares a skill: "Commit it so your team gets it too".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "When two skills share a name, the location decides".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "When two skills share a name, the location decides", so one copy wins and the other is not merged.

quizzes.stem: Two Claude sessions edit two different features in the same checkout, and each keeps overwriting the other's files. Which setup fits best?

options.a: Let the sessions take turns, committing to main after each change
options.b: Ask each session to avoid files that the other is likely to touch
options.c: Switch both sessions to plan mode so that neither writes until approved
options.d: Give every run a separate worktree, each one placed on a branch of its own

explanation.d: "Each git worktree is a separate checkout on its own branch" (module 40, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the rule is "Commit on a branch, never on main".
explanation.b: Ruled out because memory text is only context: "Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration".
explanation.c: Ruled out because plan mode only delays the writes: "Claude reads files and proposes a plan but makes no edits until you approve".

quizzes.stem: A reply begins with a confident wrong figure, and the rest of the answer then builds on it without any correction. What explains this?

options.a: The model consults a stored draft of the whole answer and then defends that draft
options.b: Each later piece is chosen with the earlier text in view, so the slip becomes context
options.c: The window dropped the opening lines, so the model lost track of what it had said
options.d: A hidden checker reviews each sentence and approves it before the sentence is shown

explanation.b: The page says "An answer is a long chain of single choices, each made with everything before it in view" (module 1, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "There is no plan stored somewhere and no lookup of a finished answer".
explanation.c: Ruled out because every choice is "made with everything before it in view", so the opening lines are still there.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the loop is only "The model computes, for every token it knows, how likely it is to come next", with no review step in it.

quizzes.stem: A team sends an entire 800,000-token archive with every request because the window allows it, and answers worsen while bills climb. Which two statements describe the problem? (Select two.)

options.a: Recall degrades as the space fills
options.b: A larger window restores accuracy, since more room means better recall
options.c: Lowering the effort speeds up processing of the extra tokens
options.d: Repeating the key instruction inside the archive fixes the drift
options.e: Extra capacity is no reason to use it all

explanation.a: "A bigger window is capacity, not a reason to send everything" (module 4, page 1), and "accuracy and recall degrade as the window fills".
explanation.e: "A bigger window is capacity, not a reason to send everything" (module 4, page 1), and "accuracy and recall degrade as the window fills".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "accuracy and recall degrade as the window fills".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "cost grows with every token you send", whatever the effort.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "more context isn't automatically better".

quizzes.stem: A system prompt contains an API key and tells Claude it is a guard who must never reveal it. A tester extracts the key with a clever request. Which redesign fits best?

options.a: Remove the credential from the context and protect it in program logic
options.b: Strengthen the role line, saying the guard is the best in the world
options.c: Add a second line that repeats the instruction in capital letters
options.d: Split the key into two halves placed in different turns of the conversation

explanation.a: "protecting a secret is a job for code" (module 6, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a role is a request, not a credential".
explanation.c: Ruled out because such a line "is a request that can be argued around".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a role is not a safeguard", and both halves still sit in the context.

quizzes.stem: A classification prompt carries five examples. Some show the label alone and others wrap it in a sentence, and live replies now vary in the same way. Which change fits best?

options.a: Add more sentence-style samples so that this style outweighs the other one
options.b: Drop every sample and rely on the written instruction to fix the shape
options.c: Rewrite every sample answer so that all of them share one identical layout
options.d: Wrap every sample in extra tags so that the model separates them better

explanation.c: The page states the course's own rule to "keep the format consistent across examples, since the model will copy inconsistencies" (module 6, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the count is not the problem: "Include 3-5 examples for best results."
explanation.b: Ruled out because multi-shot is for when "The task has subtle boundaries, or the format is unusual".
explanation.d: Ruled out because tags only mark examples as "wrapped in <example> tags", so that they are distinguished from instructions, and they do not change what the answers look like.

quizzes.stem: A support prompt is one long paragraph, and reviewers cannot tell which piece of it causes made-up verdicts when the policy is silent. Which change fits best?

options.a: Give the assistant a flattering role so that it feels bound to be careful
options.b: Separate the parts, then add a fallback value and a test for it
options.c: Ask for a longer reply in which the model explains its reasoning at length
options.d: Move the documents below the task so that the policy is read last

explanation.b: The page treats the prompt "like a short contract" whose parts are each checkable, with a constraint for the silent case and a test for it (module 6, page 3).
explanation.a: is ruled out because, as module 6, page 1 puts it, "A role is a request, not a credential".
explanation.c: Ruled out because what must hold is stated as a constraint: "use only the policy; if the policy does not decide the case, say", and a longer reply pins nothing down.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "Order: material first, the task last".

quizzes.stem: A team plans to use the token-counting tool before each message request and worries that those calls will use up the allowance for its message calls. What should the review say?

options.a: Counting needs a paid tier of its own before it can be used at all in a live service
options.b: Counting is unlimited, so it can be called as often as needed without any pacing
options.c: They are limited separately and independently, though the pre-check has its own cap
options.d: Both draw on one allowance, so each count spends a message request

explanation.c: The endpoint's own limits are stated: "it has its own limits" (module 18, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Token counting is free to use".
explanation.b: Ruled out because it is "subject to requests per minute rate limits based on your usage tier".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Token counting and message creation have separate and independent rate limits".

quizzes.stem: A feature returns a short label, and the team wants it to appear sooner. It proposes fast mode on Claude Opus 5.5. Which two statements should the review make? (Select two.)

options.a: Fast mode also lowers latency to the first token for any interactive feature
options.b: Fast mode applies once the work moves to the Message Batches API
options.c: Time to the first word barely changes
options.d: Fast mode is free on Opus 5.5 and needs only a beta header
options.e: Its benefit is tokens per second once streaming begins

explanation.c: "A feature that waits for the first word gains little" (module 19, page 2), because fast mode raises output speed and not the time to the first token.
explanation.e: "A feature that waits for the first word gains little" (module 19, page 2), because fast mode raises output speed and not the time to the first token.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Speed benefits are focused on output tokens per second (OTPS), not time to first token (TTFT)".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Fast mode is not available with the Batch API".
explanation.d: Ruled out because it is priced "twice the standard $4 and $20".

quizzes.stem: A team avoids adding a second `cache_control` entry to its prompt, believing each extra entry is billed on its own. What should the review say?

options.a: Each marker is billed at the input price, on top of the tokens it covers
