options.b: A marker is billed once per request, whether or not the prefix is reused
options.c: A marker costs nothing by itself; billing covers tokens written, read and left uncached
options.d: Markers are free, but only the first one placed in a request can ever be read

explanation.c: "Marking costs nothing by itself" (module 20, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "You pay for what is written, what is read and what is neither".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Cache breakpoints themselves don't add any cost".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "You can place up to four" explicit breakpoints, each of which can be read.

quizzes.stem: A nightly job sends 8 million input tokens and 2 million output tokens to Claude Sonnet 5.5, whose standard prices are $2 per million input and $10 per million output. What does the job cost as a batch?

explanation.b: Batch usage is charged at half, and "it is the same ratio at any size" (module 21, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because that halves only the output, but "The discount covers input, output and special tokens".
explanation.c: Ruled out because that is the standard price, and "at the standard $2 and $10 they cost $90" in the page's own case, twice the batch figure.
explanation.d: Ruled out because that halves only the input, yet "All usage is charged at 50% of the standard API prices".

quizzes.stem: A router asks a cheap model to classify each question, then maps the reply to a prompt. One reply comes back as 'Refunds?', which matches no route, and the request crashes. Which fix fits best?

options.a: Normalise the text, look it up, and send anything unknown to a default branch
options.b: Retry the classification up to five times until the reply matches a known route
options.c: Let the model add a new route whenever its reply names an unknown label
options.d: Run every question through all routes in parallel and keep the first reply

explanation.a: "A router must normalize the model's reply and have a default route" (module 34, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The model's reply is text, so it may carry a capital letter, a full stop or a word nobody planned", and a retry can repeat it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because workflows are "orchestrated through predefined code paths", so the routes are fixed by the program.
explanation.d: Ruled out because routing "directs it to a specialized followup task", one task and not all of them.

quizzes.stem: An orchestrator splits a task into three subtasks, and all three workers throw errors. The last step is asked to merge the results and writes a confident answer. What should the program do instead?

options.a: Run the last step anyway, but tell it to mention that some work failed
options.b: Retry each worker in a loop until at least one of them returns a result
options.c: Skip that stage and flag the whole job as failed, with nothing produced for the user
options.d: Return the plan text as the answer, since it already describes the work

explanation.c: "when every worker failed, nothing is combined" (module 34, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a synthesis over no results is a made-up answer".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a loop with no maximum on its iterations is an open bill".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A model's plan is text", and not a result.

quizzes.stem: A service stops reading an agent run's messages the moment the closing summary message arrives, and a few late items never reach its logs. Which change fits best?

options.a: Raise max_turns so that the run produces its late items before the closing message
options.b: Switch to partial-message events so that nothing arrives after the result
options.c: Resume the session by its identifier to fetch the missing items afterwards
options.d: Iterate to the end of the stream, since trailing events still follow the result

explanation.d: The page says to "iterate the stream to the end instead of breaking at the result" (module 35, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the limit counts tool-use turns only, "so the final text-only answer is not counted".
explanation.b: Ruled out because partial messages only add "the stream event (only when partial messages are enabled)".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the identifier "lets you resume a conversation later with the earlier context restored", and does not replay events.

quizzes.stem: A team wires its audit rule into the permission callback of its agent, yet calls to its read tools never appear in the audit log. Which two statements describe the cause and the fix? (Select two.)

options.a: Registering a second callback makes it run before the first
options.b: Anything allowed in advance skips it
options.c: An earlier hook is the place that sees everything
options.d: Switching the mode to bypass sends every call to the callback
options.e: The callback runs only for denied calls, so a deny rule must fire first

explanation.b: "Auto-approved tools never reach canUseTool", and "To gate every call, use a `PreToolUse` hook" (module 35, page 2).
explanation.c: "Auto-approved tools never reach canUseTool", and "To gate every call, use a `PreToolUse` hook" (module 35, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the callback sees only what nothing earlier decided".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a call that "bypassPermissions approved skips the callback".
explanation.e: Ruled out because "An allow rule approves a call before the callback is consulted".

quizzes.stem: An agent's safety relies on beginning with a particular permission setting, and a refactor drops the line that sets it. The unit checks of the policy function still pass. Which kind of run would catch the change?

options.a: Start the stand-in binary and read the mode back from the flags it received
options.b: Add more unit checks of the policy function, covering unusual tool names
options.c: Call the live model once per release and watch which mode each run shows
options.d: Rely on the SDK default, since it always matches the intended level

explanation.a: "Set the permission mode in the options and read it back from the flags in a test" (module 35, page 3).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "decide can be right while build_options leaves an allow list in".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The tests never call a model", which keeps them repeatable.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "If you omit it, the session can start in auto mode".

quizzes.stem: A hosted agent's shell command prints about 400,000 characters. What does the model receive for that output?

options.a: The full text, sent in several consecutive events until it is complete
options.b: Nothing, since the output is not kept once the tool call has ended
options.c: A truncated preview, with the path of a file in the sandbox that holds the rest
options.d: An error result, because any output above the limit is rejected outright by the harness

explanation.c: "the model gets a truncated preview with the path" (module 36, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because an output past the limit "is automatically written to a file in the sandbox".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Event history is persisted server-side and can be fetched in full".
explanation.d: Ruled out because such an output "is automatically written to a file in the sandbox" instead of being rejected.

quizzes.stem: A security review expects a new sandbox for a hosted agent to be cut off from the internet, because the create request never mentions the network field. What will happen?

options.a: The platform applies limited networking with an empty host list
options.b: The create request is rejected with a 400 until networking is set
options.c: Each session inherits the networking of the previous session's environment
options.d: Omission means unrestricted access, apart from a general safety blocklist

explanation.d: "a create request that omits it gets `unrestricted`" (module 36, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because limited mode must be chosen, and it "Restricts sandbox network access to the hosts in `allowed_hosts`".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "an omitted field is not neutral", but it is accepted and read as unrestricted.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "each session gets its own isolated sandbox (a fresh Linux container)".

quizzes.stem: A typed agent's reply does not fit its declared output type. What does this style do next?

options.a: It accepts the reply and flags the record for a later human review by the team
options.b: It sends the validation error back to the model as a retry and the run continues
options.c: It ends the run at once and raises an exception to the caller
options.d: It repairs the record by guessing the missing fields from the earlier replies it saw

explanation.b: "the failure goes back to the model as a retry message and the run continues" (module 37, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a reply that does not validate against the output type is refused".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the design "turns a malformed reply into a recoverable event".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a reply that does not validate against the output type is refused", and nothing is guessed.

quizzes.stem: A template builder leaves a blank where the document variable was not supplied, and the model answers confidently about nothing. Which behaviour fits best?

options.a: Fill the blank with a default document so that the model always has material
options.b: Send the request anyway and ask the model to say when material is missing
options.c: Retry the call and let the model recall the missing document from memory
options.d: Stop with a clear error before any request is made, saying what is absent

explanation.d: The builder "raises an error for an unfilled variable" (module 24, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A blank where a document should be gives a confident answer about nothing", and a default only hides the gap.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A missing variable is an error".
explanation.c: Ruled out because private material "is unknown to it unless you supply it in the context or give it a tool that fetches it".

quizzes.stem: A three-step pipeline over an 80,000-token contract resends the whole contract at every step, and costs run high. Step two only needs the clauses that step one found. Which two statements describe the change? (Select two.)

options.a: Delete every clause that looks unrelated to the question first
options.b: Move the contract into the system prompt of each step
options.c: Hand later stages just the extracted excerpts
options.d: Later stages then carry a much smaller load
options.e: Merge the three steps into one prompt so the contract goes once

explanation.c: "Pass forward only what the next step needs" (module 24, page 2), which shrinks what later stages carry.
explanation.d: "Pass forward only what the next step needs" (module 24, page 2), which shrinks what later stages carry.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the method is to "ask Claude to quote relevant parts of the documents first", not to delete by guesswork.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Each step costs the full input again" wherever the text sits.
explanation.e: Ruled out because chaining is kept to "inspect intermediate outputs or enforce a specific pipeline structure".

quizzes.stem: A service inserts a fresh random property into the shape of its JSON output format on every request, and every call shows added latency on first use. Which change fits best?

options.a: Keep the schema fixed, because compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours
options.b: Rename the schema's fields on every request so the cache sees a fresh entry
options.c: Switch to strict tool use, which skips grammar compilation entirely
options.d: Send each schema once an hour from a scheduled job so the cache stays warm

explanation.a: "A schema that changes on every request therefore never benefits from it" (module 25, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Changing only `name` or `description` fields does not invalidate the cache", so renaming gains nothing.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The cache is invalidated when the schema's structure changes or the set of tools changes".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours from last use", and the changing shape defeats any warm-up.

quizzes.stem: A hard document keeps failing validation, and the extraction loop keeps re-prompting for hours, with the bill growing each time. Which change fits best?

options.a: Raise the temperature setting so that a later attempt differs from earlier ones
options.b: Re-prompt with only the original prompt, since the error list distracts the model
options.c: Cap the attempts, then report the outcome with its last problems for a person
options.d: Remove the validation step for that document so that the first reply is accepted

explanation.c: "An unbounded retry on a hard document is a cost leak" (module 25, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because current models "do not support setting temperature".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the model has no way to know what was wrong" without it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a parse that succeeds "says nothing about the content".

quizzes.stem: A team wants to prepend a short context sentence to each of its 50,000 chunks before indexing, but fears the model calls would be too costly. Which fact answers the worry?

options.a: The sentences are generated once per chunk for free, since indexing is not billed
options.b: Contextual retrieval needs no extra calls, since the embeddings already hold the context
options.c: Only the first thousand chunks need a sentence, since later ones inherit it
options.d: Caching the document makes the work affordable, at about a dollar per million tokens

explanation.d: The write-up says to "make contextualization affordable with prompt caching" (module 28, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The model is asked to write that sentence for each chunk, with the whole document in view".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A chunk lifted out of its document can lose its meaning".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the fix is to prepend "chunk-specific explanatory context to each chunk before embedding".

quizzes.stem: A team asks Claude in the prompt to quote its sources for each claim, and the replies get expensive. Which feature addresses this?

options.a: The Files API, which stores the quoted material outside the request
options.b: Citations, whose cited text is not counted toward output tokens
options.c: Structured outputs, which compress each quote into a fixed shape
options.d: A prompt rule asking for shorter quotes of ten words at most

explanation.b: "`cited_text` does not count toward your output tokens" (module 29, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "File content used in Messages requests is priced as input tokens".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Citations and structured outputs are incompatible".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "citations are guaranteed to contain valid pointers to the provided documents", which a prompt rule is not.

quizzes.stem: An assistant keeps calling a tool that keeps failing, and the loop, which only watches the stop reason, runs until the budget is gone. Which two changes fit? (Select two.)

options.a: Make the handler return an empty string so the tool seems to succeed
options.b: Wait for the model to decide to stop by itself
options.c: Cap the number of model calls
options.d: Report a separate outcome when the cap is reached
options.e: Rely on the runner's default behaviour, which has no limit

explanation.c: "The loop needs its own limit of model calls, and a status for reaching it" (module 26, page 2).
explanation.d: "The loop needs its own limit of model calls, and a status for reaching it" (module 26, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A result that quietly returns an empty string for a failure teaches the model that the tool worked".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A model that keeps calling a tool that keeps failing never decides".
explanation.e: Ruled out because the runner loops "until it reaches `max_iterations`".

quizzes.stem: A migration touches hundreds of files, and the team wants its findings cross-checked before anyone sees them, which is beyond what a handful of helpers can manage. Which extension fits best?

options.a: A subagent, because Claude decides turn by turn what runs next
options.b: A skill, because it adds reference material to every conversation
options.c: A dynamic workflow, where a script rather than the model decides what runs next
options.d: A line in CLAUDE.md that tells Claude to double-check its own findings

explanation.c: "In a workflow, the script decides" (module 27, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a subagent is for "a quick, focused worker".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a skill "adds to your main window".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Claude follows both as instructions, so neither is enforced".

quizzes.stem: A new server design wants to borrow the host application's language model for a completion, so that the server needs no key of its own. What does the 2026-07-28 revision advise?

options.a: Use sampling, which is the preferred way to reuse the host's model
options.b: Integrate with a provider's API directly, since sampling is deprecated
options.c: Use roots, which let the server borrow the model through the client's paths
options.d: Use elicitation, which asks the host's model for a completion on the user's behalf

explanation.b: The advice is to "call a model provider directly instead of sampling" (module 32, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "roots and logging over the protocol are deprecated" as well, and neither supplies a completion.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Elicitation lets a server ask the user for more information", not a model.

quizzes.stem: A server test checks a refused call by demanding that the client's reply equal the handler's own sentence, and it fails because the client adds extra words at the start. Which change fits best?

options.a: Wait for an exception from the client, since errors are raised and not returned to it
options.b: Call the handler directly in the test, which returns the exact text it produced
options.c: Change the handler so that it adds the same extra words to its own sentence
options.d: Assert that the error contains the expected phrase rather than matching it whole

explanation.d: "a test checks that the message contains your text instead of comparing it whole" (module 32, page 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a test reads the flag and the text and does not wait for an exception".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A direct call does not see stray output, the schema or the transport".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "An SDK can add a prefix", and the fix belongs in the comparison.

quizzes.stem: A remote server advertises every permission it has in its metadata, and clients request all of them, so a stolen token would reach widely. Which design change fits best?

options.a: Start with a small set of low-risk read scopes and escalate by targeted challenge
options.b: Issue longer-lived tokens so that clients are asked for consent less often by the server
options.c: Keep every scope but require the token in the URL query string to track use
options.d: Drop authorization on HTTP and trust the Origin header alone

explanation.a: The guidance is "a progressive, least-privilege model" (module 33, page 2).
explanation.b: Ruled out because an everything-scope design gives "users a consent dialog nobody reads", and longer lives add risk.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Access tokens MUST NOT be included in the URI query string".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "servers should implement authentication for all connections".

quizzes.stem: A client of a Streamable HTTP server wants to cancel a long tool call it started. Which signal does the specification expect?

options.a: A cancel message naming the request, sent on a second connection
options.b: A progress token that decreases to zero to signal that work should stop
options.c: Closing the event channel that carries that reply
options.d: A GET request to a cancel endpoint of the server

explanation.c: On Streamable HTTP "Closing the SSE response stream" is the signal (module 33, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "On stdio the client sends a `notifications/cancelled` message that names the request", and that is the stdio rule.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a progress token carries "a value that must increase with each one".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the GET stream endpoint was removed" in this revision.

quizzes.stem: A compliance lead states that every Claude interaction in the company is covered by the Enterprise audit logs. One team uses the Microsoft 365 add-ins. What should the review say?

options.a: The statement holds, since the Enterprise plan logs all activity across every product
options.b: The add-ins inherit the custom retention settings, so their activity is logged for the same time
options.c: Streaming the add-in events to the monitoring tools would close the gap
options.d: Verify each product separately, since these extensions fall outside that record

explanation.d: "the Microsoft 365 add-ins are outside the Enterprise audit logs" (module 10, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "coverage is not uniform" across products.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the add-ins "do not inherit custom retention settings".
explanation.c: Ruled out because that feature is "streaming of Cowork events to the organisation's monitoring tools", not add-in events.

quizzes.stem: A production agent calls a partner service with an access secret that the team set as an environment variable inside the agent's sandbox. Which change fits best?

options.a: Rotate the secret weekly so that a leaked copy expires quickly afterwards
options.b: Keep an opaque stand-in there and let the platform swap in the real value at send time
options.c: Encrypt the variable inside the image so that just the agent process can read it
options.d: Tell the agent in its instructions to keep the secret out of its output

explanation.b: The page says that vaults store "an opaque placeholder" in the sandbox, so "The agent never sees the secret value." (module 41, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the rule for production agents is to "keep the value out of the sandbox", and rotation leaves it there.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the environment key goes in a secrets manager and never in an image".
explanation.d: Ruled out because an instruction is a request, while "A key that appears in a tool result or an audit line has left your control".

quizzes.stem: A screen-driving loop acts on just the first step of each assistant turn and sends back a single outcome. After a turn that planned click, type and click, the next call fails with a 400. Which two statements fit? (Select two.)

options.a: A smaller screenshot makes the request fit the limit
options.b: A pause between turns gives the earlier request time to finish
options.c: A longer client timeout lets the same turn go through
options.d: Every block of that message needs an answer
options.e: Unanswered items count as an invalid request

explanation.d: "Leaving a block unanswered is an `invalid_request_error`" (module 31, page 1).
explanation.e: "Leaving a block unanswered is an `invalid_request_error`" (module 31, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page ties image size to "the toolset takes no display dimensions and the API doesn't downscale for you".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Every block still needs a result", whatever the timing.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the cause is "an agent loop that reads only the first block", which a timeout leaves as it was.

quizzes.stem: A support bot's users sometimes craft inputs to bypass its rules, and the team has no record of who tried what. Which defence is missing?

options.a: A log of every attempt, so that repeat offenders get throttled or banned
options.b: A pattern list of known attack phrases, which makes logging unnecessary
options.c: Placing each user's text in the system prompt so the model gives it priority
options.d: A larger context window, so that the whole history of the attacker's inputs fits

explanation.a: "you cannot respond to a pattern you did not log" (module 41, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A list of patterns catches the phrasing someone thought of and misses the paraphrase".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "data that sits in the system prompt gets the authority of an instruction".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "more context isn't automatically better".

quizzes.stem: Claude ran a script that altered rows in a production database. The developer presses Esc twice to rewind, expecting the rows to come back. What happens?

options.a: Everything is undone, because the checkpoint also snapshots the database
options.b: The database is restored only if Claude is asked to undo the script itself
options.c: Only file edits are undone; changes made to outside systems stay in place
options.d: The rewind is refused, because a session cannot rewind after running a command

explanation.c: Checkpoints "only cover file changes" (module 38, page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Actions that affect remote systems (databases, APIs, deployments) can't be checkpointed".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Before Claude edits a file, it snapshots the current contents", and nothing is snapshotted for a database.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the command "rolls code and conversation back to a checkpoint".

quizzes.stem: A team adds a deny entry `Write(./config/prod.yaml)` to its settings, yet Claude still changes that configuration. Which fix fits best?

options.a: Move the entry from the shared file to the user file, which ranks lower
options.b: Add a line to the memory file asking Claude not to change that configuration
options.c: Replace the deny entry with an ask entry for Write, so that Claude must ask first
options.d: Use an Edit or Read rule instead, since a Write path rule is never consulted

explanation.d: "a `Write(...)` path rule is not consulted, so protect files with `Edit` or `Read` rules" (module 38, page 2).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Lists, such as the allow and deny arrays, are not replaced: they combine across layers", so the layer changes nothing.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration".
explanation.c: Ruled out because it would still be a Write rule, and "a Write(...) path rule is not consulted".

quizzes.stem: A response arrives whose stop reason is `model_context_window_exceeded`. How should the client handle it?

options.a: Treat it as truncated, then trim or compact the history before the next call
options.b: Retry the identical request on the same model, since the failure is on the service side
options.c: Raise max_tokens so that the reply has room to finish
options.d: Switch to a fallback model, since the model declined to answer

explanation.a: The page says to "Treat the response as truncated, then trim or compact the context" (module 43, page 1).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the origin is "Integration: the context is yours".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the cause is that "the response filled the model's context window", which no output ceiling widens.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the fallback is the cure for a refusal: "Read `stop_details` and retry on a fallback model".
